findings.title: stamp-refined read-back never asserts the path_label write — a rejected write still prints STAMPED
findings.evidence: The read-back (introduced by ac-heyt.7) asserts only refined-present and unrefined-absent; the third write `br label add "$id" "$path_label"` (line 210, exit discarded with `|| true`) is never re-read. Mutation probe executed in a sandbox (mock br named br on PATH, fixture bead ac-proof): baseline stamp prints `STAMPED ac-proof (refine-full)` rc 0; with the path-label add REFUSED (rc 4, board unchanged) the SAME `STAMPED` + rc 0 is printed. Downstream bead-artifact.py classifies runs by the STAMPED substring, and the LABEL-FREEZE refine-full/refine-light frequency series (beads-standards SKILL.md:237) silently under-counts. The comment at line 211 claims 'the label set the stamp meant to produce is asserted' — it is not.
findings.fix: Extend the read-back: after computing labels_now, also assert the normalized label set contains the expected side-values — e.g. fail unless the joined labels match the intended set {refined present, unrefined absent, path_label present}; a WRITE-FAILED on path_label absence gives the partial write the same exit-2 verdict the refined/unrefined writes get.

findings.title: Check 36 blind to a raw br --json read split across lines — green tree with an unenrouted call site
findings.evidence: RAW_READ and ROUTED_READ are per-line regexes; both require br and --json on the SAME line. Executed probe: a scratch tree with 13 br_call sites plus sneaky.sh containing `out=$(` / `  br list` / `  --json` — the checker prints 'ok ... 13 routed call site(s)' and exits 0, so the raw unenrouted read passes as clean. A future converted consumer written with the flag on its own line (or a python call with br and --json on separate lines, which the twin exemption also doesn't cover outside the sanctioned file) evades the D9 completeness sensor, the exact drift the check exists to make a red commit.
findings.fix: Scan per-logical-statement, not per-line: join backslash-continuations and match a windowed context (e.g. accumulate a 3-line sliding window before matching RAW_READ, or match `br`-invocation lines and then check --json appears within the next 3 lines; mirror this in the ROUTED_READ counting).

findings.title: Check 35 treats a missing created_at as pre-cutover — the origin-less open bead it guards passes
findings.evidence: `created = str(rec.get("created_at") or "")[:10]`; rule 3 fires only when `created >= CUTOVER`. Executed probe: a committed board holding only `{"id":"bd-z","status":"open","labels":[],"title":"no created_at"}` (origin-less, open) exits 0 — '1 record(s) scanned — well-formed, ids unique, open post-cutover beads origin-tagged'. The check exists precisely as a backstop for the fail-open create guards (header/no header text); a record whose created_at is absent, empty or malformed fails OPEN into 'pre-cutover' and is never scanned, recreating the hole the check was written to close.
findings.fix: Fail closed on the timestamp: if the record is open and created_at is missing or does not parse to a valid `>= CUTOVER`/earlier date (i.e. created does not match ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$ or is empty), append a violation ('open bead has no parseable created_at — cannot prove it is pre-cutover') instead of treating '' as before 2026-08-23.

findings.title: Check 35 exits 0 on a blank/newline-only ledger even though it scanned zero records
findings.evidence: The NOT-GATED guard is `if not lines` — a file containing a single newline yields lines == [''], every record is skipped by `if not line: continue`, `scanned` stays 0, violations stays empty and the code prints '0 record(s) scanned — well-formed...' and returns 0. Executed probe: a dir with .beads/issues.jsonl containing only '\n' returns rc 0. This contradicts the check's own documented exit contract ('Exit: 0 clean (at least one record scanned)') and its own premise 'a check that read nothing has proved nothing' — a truncated/blank ledger reads as a clean board.
findings.fix: Return 2 when `scanned` is 0 even if the line array is non-empty (mirroring the empty-board guard), e.g. change the final verdict to `if not violations and scanned > 0 ... else if scanned == 0: exit 2 NOT-GATED`.

findings.title: close-gate.sh and coordinator.sh resolve BR_CALL after `cd $ROOT` — their pre-cd comment is false and relative relative-path invocations break
findings.evidence: Both files compute `BR_CALL="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../_tools" ...)" AFTER the `cd "$ROOT"` (coordinator.sh:75 likewise), while the code block's own comment states 'Path computed BEFORE the cd above: BASH_SOURCE may be relative' — the sibling flight-check.sh and refly.sh genuinely source pre-cd. Executed probe: a scratch repo, invoked as `bash ../skills/ac-implement/scripts/close-gate.sh <id> --reason x` from its sub/ directory → `NOT-CHECKED: READ — br-call.sh helper missing at '/br-call.sh'` exit 2. The read now fails where the pre-diff script proceeded (pre-diff there was no helper resolution at all), turning a valid invocation into a false NOT-CHECKED. Fail-closed, but a worker lane loses a valid gate run.
findings.fix: Move the BR_CALL assignment (and the `.` sourcing) ABOVE the `cd "$ROOT"` in close-gate.sh and coordinator.sh, matching flight-check.sh/refly.sh; or resolve from a var captured before the cd. Also correct the comment when moved.

findings.title: stamp-refined writes the labels via bare `br` while every read now honors AC2_BR_CMD — the read-back can verify a different board than it wrote
findings.evidence: The conversion routes all reads through br_call (which honors AC2_BR_CMD, br-call.sh:26), but the write legs call the bare binary: lines 76-77 (downgrade remove/add) and 208-210 (remove unrefined, add refined, add path_label). br-call.sh:19's own contract says honoring the seam 'keeps a converted caller's read and write on the SAME binary when the seam is set' — this converted caller breaks exactly that. With AC2_BR_CMD set (a different board/binary, e.g. a mirror or the harness shims this registry already uses — the FRICTIONS ledger at bd-edw72 records this identical read/write split in close-evidence-check), the read-back evaluates a different board than the three writes targeted, so a verified-looking stamp can be verified against the wrong board, and bead-artifact.py (close-gate.sh:364 deliberately passes the seam) subclasses the run by that STAMPED line.
findings.fix: Use the same seam for the writes: honor ${AC2_BR_CMD:-br} for the five br label calls (or export AC2_BR_CMD="${AC2_BR_CMD:-br}" and invoke via br_call-style wrapper covering writes; at minimum write with "$BR"/"${AC2_BR_CMD:-br}" like close-gate.sh's BR variable).

findings.title: Dispatcher fail-closed notice dereferences output.parts without the hedge its own next line applies
findings.evidence: In the wire-rendered plugin, the chat.message WIRING_ERROR branch does `const base = (output.parts || [])[0] || {}` then `output.parts.push({...})` — if output.parts is ever absent, the push throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined' inside the handler, so the designed fail-closed notice never lands (and the handler crashes instead of injecting text). Two lines later the normal path of the SAME function hedges `const parts = output.parts || []`, and parts.push there would push onto a LOCAL copy — the same silent-loss shape — so the file is internally inconsistent about whether parts may be undefined. This branch is the D-1 layer-disappearance announcement; its failure mode is exactly the silent-degradation class it was written to prevent.
findings.fix: Hedge consistently: `const parts = (output.parts ||= [])` (or `output.parts = output.parts || []`) before building base and pushing, in BOTH the WIRING_ERROR branch and the normal chat.message path, so the injected text lands on the payload opencode actually reads.
